propositions: Recovery preflight rejects contexts exceeding a flat 100,000-char bound even when the assembled product (context_chars × criteria_count) remains within the ratified worst-case ceiling (3.2M chars for 32 criteria).

The flat per-context bound conflates two independent ceilings: physical (context must fit one model inference window) and economic (recovery multiplies context_chars by criteria_count); raising the flat bound chases a monotonically growing tail.

Recovery input validation must derive the physical ceiling from the resolved verifier model's own context window (via MODEL_LADDER), not a fixed constant, and enforce the economic ceiling as a product bound (context_chars × criteria_count ≤ 3,200,000).

The live c9f7 ticket (121,147 char context, 22 criteria, 2.67M product) is refused at preflight under the old bound but should be admitted under a window-derived physical ceiling and product-based economic ceiling.
The criteria budget invariant (_MAX_TOTAL_CRITERIA_CHARS ≤ physical_context_ceiling) and full-context byte-identical transmission must be preserved; no context elision on refusal.

The economic ceiling is explicitly interim, modeling per-criterion fan-out that will be replaced by banked-verification batching; shipping the interim bound unblocks re-certifications refused at preflight today.
